items.title: Bus hits train stopped on French side of Channel Tunnel, with 19 injured
items.description: Two people were severely injured and evacuated by helicopter but no one's life appeared to be in danger, officials said.

items.title: Trump calls off livestream of Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad
items.description: Trump said some would "rather not watch" the killing of Nidal Hasan, the first military execution in over 60 years.

items.title: Russia accuses Ukraine of attacking oil refinery after Zelensky says strikes to resume
items.description: Ukraine's president says a pause on striking energy sites is over following fresh Russian attacks.

items.title: Maduro pleads not guilty to new torture-related charges in New York
items.description: "I reject this document entirely," Maduro said in court, responding to newly added torture-related charges.

items.title: At least 33 pupils and teacher killed after school roof collapses in Pakistan
items.description: Children were buried under the debris after the roof crashed through three classrooms, police say.

items.title: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills two, minister says
items.description: Yemen's information minister says the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace.

items.title: Was Neanderthal life violent? This wound suggests lethal fighting was more common
items.description: A 75,000-year-old Neanderthal spear wound may be evidence violence shaped human life far earlier than thought.

items.title: Seven crew missing after drone attack leaves tanker ablaze off Romania's coast
items.description: A search and rescue operation is under way in the Black Sea after the latest attack in the area.

items.title: White House defends new press secretary over her legal credentials
items.description: Katie Zacharia does not appear to be registered to the legal bar in any state where she has lived.

items.title: School headscarf ban sparks rare protests in Azerbaijan and row with Turkey
items.description: Protests have taken place over the rules which have seen pupils wearing hijabs turned away from schools.

items.title: Letters with 'suspicious substances' sent to US election offices
items.description: A number of states have confirmed they were targeted by the mailings, including Oklahoma, Ohio and Louisiana.

items.title: Two dead in Istanbul after heaviest rainfall in 84 years, governor says
items.description: Residents have been told to avoid leaving their homes unless absolutely necessary.

items.title: Obama says drift towards extremism 'not inevitable'
items.description: More than 12,000 people filled a major venue in the city to hear the former US president's take on the challenges the world is facing. .

items.title: Brazil's Congress approves shorter working week in win for Lula
items.description: Lula's supporters hope the measure will boost his popularity ahead of a presidential run-off in 10 days.

items.title: At the Brooklyn shop in 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird
items.description: Art of Play says its staff have been threatened after the singer complained online about how she was treated.

items.title: Actor Imran Khan ordered to leave India after participating in protest
items.description: The Bollywood actor had been detained and released while participating in a protest in Mumbai on 10 October.

items.title: Australian woman charged with lacing colleague's curry with snail poison
items.description: The alleged victim, who was in a relationship with the woman, had spotted bright green pellets in the meal.

items.title: North Korea and China open new bridge after 12-year delay
items.description: China is the North's largest trading partner and a lifeline against the sanctions Pyongyang faces.

items.title: Indian woman and boyfriend get death sentence in 'blue drum' murder case
items.description: The body was recovered from a large blue plastic storage container - locally called a drum.

items.title: Student protesters attack government buildings in Albania
items.description: Buildings were set alight on the second day of demonstrations from thousands of students who want better university conditions and job prospects.
